when: Teaching card, right after Play, before the opening
text: Welcome, mission engineer! Walk with W, A, S, D and look around with the mouse. Or click on the floor, and you’ll walk there.

when: The opening scene, once the welcome card has closed
text: Good evening, astronauts! Tonight I’m going to give you a short briefing about your mission. Follow me to the briefing room.

when: The opening scene
text: Finally! It’s the day we’ve been dreaming about. We’ll be on the Moon soon!

scene: Scene 2: the walk to the briefing room
when: Walking to the briefing room, the crew walking along
text: For those who don’t know me yet: I’m your trainer. For months I’ve taught you how to fly, how to fix things, and how to stay calm when things go wrong.

scene: Scene 2: the walk to the briefing room
when: Walking to the briefing room, the crew walking along
text: My job ends at the launch pad. After that, your crew and Houston will look after you.

scene: Scene 2: the walk to the briefing room
when: Walking to the briefing room, the crew walking along
text: He says that every year. Then he watches every launch with his fingers crossed.

scene: Scene 2: the walk to the briefing room
when: Teaching card, on first reaching the corridor
text: Lost? Press G any time for your guidebook: space words, where your tasks are, and every key.

scene: Scene 2: the walk to the briefing room
when: On reaching the briefing room
text: Guilty. Here we are.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Take a seat. I’ll start the mission briefing in a moment.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Tonight, your rocket carries the four of you from Earth to the Moon.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: You’ll spend a few days in space on the way.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Then you land near the Moon’s south pole and wake up our outpost. It has been asleep, waiting for you.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Up there, you’ll have to keep the power on, the air clean, the plants growing, and the radio talking to Earth.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: And you’ll have to make hard choices. Something that helps you today might cost you tomorrow. There’s rarely one perfect answer.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Which is why we listen to each other before we decide.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: And once we decide, we stick together.

when: The briefing scene, starting by itself after “Here we are” (before task 1)
text: Your first real decision. The outpost needs a power source, and our mission engineer gets to choose it. Listen to your crew first.

when: Task panel: Choose the power source (advice)
text: Solar panels are light. That leaves more room for cargo!

when: Task panel: Choose the power source (advice)
text: Houston here. Moon nights last two weeks. Solar panels go dark.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Not so fast! Choose your power source in the briefing room first.

when: After task 1
text: Good. Remember that choice. You’ll find out on the Moon how it works out.

when: After task 1
text: That’s all for the briefing. Before you do anything else, why doesn’t our mission engineer pay one last visit to the communications officer? He’ll be your voice from Earth.

when: After task 1
text: Go on. I’ll save you a seat on the rocket.

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: At his door
text: There’s our mission engineer! Good luck tonight, astronaut. Today you leave Earth and head out into space.

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: At his door
text: And I’ll be right here the whole way. I’ll stay connected to your team by radio. If anything goes wrong, any problem at all, I’ll be the first one to help.

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: At his door
text: So tell me. Have you checked your cargo for the trip?

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: If you say you haven’t checked the cargo
text: Then let’s fix that. Every kilogram on that rocket matters, so head to the cargo hangar and pack it yourself.

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: If you say you have
text: That’s the spirit. Good astronauts always check twice. The cargo hangar is next door.

scene: Scene 4: Houston at the communications building
when: At his door
text: I’ll call you on the radio when you’re done.

when: On first walking into the hangar
text: Thought you’d end up here. The rocket can only carry so much, so we can’t take everything. You pick.

when: Task panel: Pack the cargo (advice)
text: Houston here. Pack spares. Things always break, and we can’t send parts quickly.

when: Task panel: Pack the cargo (advice)
text: Every block of spares is a block less shielding.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
text: Hold on, astronaut. Pack the cargo in the hangar first.

when: In the cargo panel, when a block won’t fit
text: It’s full! Put something back if you want that one.

when: After packing
text: Packed and sealed. No changing your mind now!

scene: Scene 6: Houston’s call and the goodbye
when: After packing
text: Houston here. I see your cargo is loaded. Nice work, mission engineer.

scene: Scene 6: Houston’s call and the goodbye
when: After packing
text: The rocket is fuelled and ready. Head to the launch pad and take the elevator up to the hatch. Your crew is waiting.

scene: Scene 6: Houston’s call and the goodbye
when: The goodbye at the crew elevator
text: This is where I leave you. You’ve trained hard for this. Trust your crew, think before you choose, and bring everyone home.

scene: Scene 6: Houston’s call and the goodbye
when: The goodbye at the crew elevator
text: Now go. The Moon is waiting.

when: After unbuckling, once per run
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Welcome to microgravity, {name}! Push off gently. Nothing weighs anything up here.

when: After unbuckling, once per run
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Our safety officer is in life support, at the back. Go and help.

when: Before the panel (the ask)
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Hey {name}, the air scrubber is failing. Can you help me decide?

when: Task panel: Scrubber fault (advice)
text: Swap in a spare part and fix it properly.

when: Task panel: Scrubber fault (advice)
text: Switch to the backup. It’s quick, but it uses power.

when: On the locked option “Repair it”
text: We’d fix this in minutes if we’d packed spares.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: The air scrubber needs fixing before we land.

when: After a good choice
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: That did it. The air is clean again. Thank you!

when: After a risky choice
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: We’ll manage. But stuffy air will make us all tired.

when: The hand-off to the cockpit
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Good work. Come up to the cockpit. We need to pick where to land.

when: The alert, with no warning first
text: Solar storm! The radiation is coming. Decide fast.

when: Houston’s warning (or call) before the panel
text: Houston here. A flare just went off. Get to the shelter soon.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit (advice)
text: Everyone into the shelter. The repair can wait.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit (advice)
text: If we stop now, we’ll have to start the repair again.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit, second time
text: Another flare. Same drill: into the shelter.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit, second time
text: Again? We’ll never finish this repair at this rate.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit, third time
text: A third storm. Nobody takes chances this time.

when: Task panel: Storm in transit, third time
text: We’re so close. Can two of us keep going?

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
text: Houston here. No storms on our screens right now.

when: In the result, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Without the shielding we left behind, this cabin is thin.

when: After sheltering everyone
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: That was close. I’m glad we all fit in there.

when: After sheltering part of the crew
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Those of us outside took a dose. Let’s be more careful.

when: After working through it
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: The repair is done, but we all took radiation. It adds up.

when: Before the panel (the ask)
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: {name}, help me pick where we land. Our outpost is already waiting down there.

when: Task panel: Pick the landing site (advice)
text: Stay close to the ice. We can turn it into water!

when: Task panel: Pick the landing site (advice)
text: We need sunlight too. Our panels run on it.

when: On picking “Sunny ridge”, which the crew rules out
text: The ridge is too far from the ice. Our outpost is waiting on the slope between. Let’s land there.

when: On picking “Crater rim”, which the crew rules out
text: The crater rim is in shadow too often for our panels. Our outpost is on the slope between. We land there.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: We can’t land until we pick a landing site.

when: After choosing, before the landing
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Strap in. We’re going down.

when: Off the lander (a scene, once per profile)
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Welcome to the Moon, {name}. The airlock is this way.

when: Inside, after the airlock
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Welcome home, {name}. First job: wake the base. The power bay is this way.

when: Before the panel (the ask)
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: The base is asleep. You share out our power, {name}. Choose well.

when: Task panel: Wake the base (advice)
text: Life support first. Always.

when: Task panel: Wake the base (advice)
text: Without the greenhouse, we’ll run out of food.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Wake the base in the power bay first.

when: After the task
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Lights on, air flowing. Nice work.

when: The hand-off to the greenhouse
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: {name}! Come to the greenhouse. I need your help!

when: Before the panel (the ask)
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: {name}! The greenhouse is ready, but water is tight. What should we plant?

when: Task panel: Greenhouse (advice)
text: Plant everything! We’ll be glad of fresh food later.

when: Task panel: Greenhouse (advice)
text: Water is life support. Save it until we know we have enough.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: We haven’t planted the greenhouse yet.

when: After planting
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Seeds in! We’ll have fresh food before long.

when: After saving the water
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: No seeds this time. I hope our food lasts.

when: The hand-off to crew quarters
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Can you come to crew quarters? The crew needs you.

when: Before the panel (the ask)
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: The crew is worn out, {name}. What should we do?

when: Task panel: Tired crew (advice)
text: Everyone needs a full day of rest. Tired people make mistakes.

when: Task panel: Tired crew (advice)
text: We still have to finish the roof before the next storm.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: The crew needs a decision about rest first.

when: After resting
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Thank you. Rested people make fewer mistakes.

when: After pushing on
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: We’ll push on. Watch for anyone who looks too tired.

when: On a night card, about the day (in turn)
text: Long day. The plants look happy, though.

when: On a night card, about the day (in turn)
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Everyone is tucked in. Get some sleep, {name}.

when: On a night card, about the day (in turn)
text: Another day done. Tomorrow we keep going.

when: On a night card, about the day (in turn)
text: Houston here. Good night, outpost. We’re watching over you.

when: On the night card, when an earlier choice comes back
text: That would be an easy fix with a spare part.

when: On the night card, when an earlier choice comes back
text: We’re down to our last meals. More supplies would have helped.

when: On the night card, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Pushing on wore our botanist out. She has to rest now.

when: On the night card, when an earlier choice comes back
text: We never planted. There’s no fresh food for the night.

when: On the night card: the briefing that opens task 8
text: We need water. There’s ice in the crater to the east.

when: On the night card, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Rationing water is wearing us down. We should have brought ice back.

when: When the radiation dose reaches the moderate level
delivery: in the result or on the night card
text: Radiation dose means how much radiation our bodies have soaked up. Ours is getting high. No more risks.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: On the drive, at the home line
text: You have just enough charge to get home. Turn back now.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: If the rover’s battery runs flat (the tow)
text: We’ve lost the rover out there. From now on we walk.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: At the crater, before the panel
text: Look at all that ice! How much should we take?

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: Task panel: Rover drive and water ice (advice)
text: Dig out as much as we can. Ice means water and air!

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: Task panel: Rover drive and water ice (advice)
text: Every minute out here adds radiation. Take a little and go.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Not yet. Wait for my briefing at command.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: After taking ice
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Water from the Moon! Bring it home safely.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: After leaving it
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: No ice for now. We’ll have to save water.

scene: Task 8: the rover and the ice
when: The hand-off back to base
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: Head back to base, {name}. The long night is coming.

when: Houston’s warning (or call) before the panel
text: Houston here. We’re seeing a big flare on the Sun. Particles could reach you soon.

when: Task panel: Solar storm (advice)
text: Everyone to the shelter, now!

when: Task panel: Solar storm (advice)
text: The roof is almost finished. A few more minutes and we’re done!

when: Task panel: Solar storm, second time
text: Another storm! Everyone to the shelter.

when: Task panel: Solar storm, second time
text: We lost a whole day last time. Can we keep working?

when: Task panel: Solar storm, third time
text: Third storm. Our dose keeps adding up. Shelter now.

when: Task panel: Solar storm, third time
text: The Sun won’t stop. We still have a base to run.

when: In the result, when an earlier choice comes back
text: We took a dose on the way here. We can’t take much more.

when: In the result, when an earlier choice comes back
text: We left the shielding on Earth. This is going to hurt.

when: In the result, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Houston couldn’t reach us.

when: In the result of “Keep working”, when an earlier choice comes back
text: My head hurts. I should have sheltered.

when: After sheltering everyone
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Safe in here. Thanks for getting us all inside.

when: After not sheltering everyone
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: That storm hit us hard. Next time, we all shelter.

when: The alert
text: Something just hit a solar panel. Let’s look at the damage.

when: After the alert, before the panel
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: A panel has been hit, {name}. How should we fix it?

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel (advice)
text: Let’s walk out and swap the part. We need full power for the night.

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel (advice)
text: A moonwalk uses air and adds radiation. Patch it from here.

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel, second time
text: Another hit! Let’s swap the part before power drops more.

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel, second time
text: Every walk out adds radiation. A patch will do.

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel, third time
text: A third panel down. We need full power for the night.

when: Task panel: Broken solar panel, third time
text: We’ve been out so much already. Patch it from here.

when: On the locked option “Moonwalk to replace it”
text: That would be an easy fix with a spare part.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: The solar panels are working fine for now.

when: In the result of “Moonwalk to replace it”, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Without the rover, it’s a long walk out there.

when: In the result of “Patch it”, when an earlier choice comes back
text: On foot, even a short trip adds up.

when: After replacing the part
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Good as new. We’ll need that power tonight.

when: After patching it
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: It will hold. Half power is better than none.

when: After leaving it
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Less power, then. We’ll have to be careful tonight.

when: The commander’s story at the window (a scene, once per profile)
text: On my first mission, I took a risk to save time.

when: The commander’s story at the window (a scene, once per profile)
text: We got home. But I learned: plan for the long night.

when: After the story, before the panel
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
note: says the player’s name ({name}); the recording says “astronaut” there
text: The long night is coming, {name}. How do we get through it?

when: Houston’s warning (or call) before the panel
text: Houston here. It’s going to be a long, cold night. Save what you can.

when: Task panel: Lunar night falls (advice)
text: Turn almost everything off and sleep through it.

when: Task panel: Lunar night falls (advice)
text: Keep everything running. The crew has to stay warm and well.

when: If you try this task too early, or ask what’s left
delivery: in person, or hologram if they’re elsewhere
text: Not yet. We have work to do before nightfall.

when: In the result, when an earlier choice comes back
text: Solar panels make nothing in the dark. A reactor would have kept us going.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Good endings
text: You kept a cool head and a safety margin. I’d fly with you again.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Early returns
text: Coming home early is not failing. We all get home, and next time we plan better.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Good endings
text: Nobody got hurt. That’s the best report a safety officer can write.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Early returns
text: Sending everyone home was the right call. The crew always comes first.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Good endings
text: We grew food on the Moon! I can’t wait to tell everyone back home.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Early returns
text: We learned a lot, even if it was hard. That’s what science is for.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Good endings
text: Houston here. Great work up there. Everyone down here is cheering.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Early returns
text: Houston here. We’re bringing you home. You did everything you could.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Good endings
text: Your choices back on Earth paid off on the Moon. That’s what training is for.

scene: The closing line (from whoever’s advice you followed most)
when: Early returns
text: Every trade-off you made taught you something. Let’s train again.
